articleTitle: Automotive Gear Defect Detection Method based on Yolov8 Algorithm
abstract: For the problem of low efficiency and accuracy of automotive gear defect detection by manual visual inspection method, a detection method of automotive gear endface defects based on Yolov8s algorithm is proposed. The original Yolov8s model is improved in this paper considering the problem of smaller defects in automotive gears. Firstly, the CBAM attention mechanism was introduced in Backbone to help the model pay more attention to information related to gear defects while suppressing useless information in the data. It better captures the key features of gear defects. Secondly, a small target detection layer is added to the network structure to solve the problem of small target information loss due to the large downsampling multiplier of Yolov8s. It better extracts the features of small targets. For the problem that some defective kinds of samples in the dataset collected from real industrial scenes are too small, this paper uses the Mosaic data augmentation method, which is used to expand the number of samples and solve the problem of inadequate training to some extent. The improved Yolov8s was compared with the original Yolov8s model for experiments. The results show that the improved Yolov8s model improves both Precision and Recall over the original Yolov8s model. Meanwhile, the improved Yolov8 algorithm is used for automotive gear defect detection in a real scenario detection task, which effectively reduces the miss detection rate and shows good performance. It meets the inspection needs of real industrial scenarios, and is advanced and practical in automotive gear defect detection.

articleTitle: Facial expression recognition using LBP and CNN networks integrating attention mechanism
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of facial expression recognition, a novel method integrating attention mechanism on LBP and CNN networks is proposed, and verified on public datasets. The self-built attention mechanism can help the model automatically select and focus attention on the most informative areas in the image, so as to improve the recognition performance of the model for key areas, and then improve the accuracy of recognition. Firstly, the public dataset is preprocessed. Local Binary Pattern (LBP) is used to obtain local texture features. The resulting dataset of LBP features is randomly scrambled multiple times. The attention mechanism is embedded in the CNN, and the Adam optimizer is used to train and verify the scrambled dataset every time. The FER2013 dataset, CK dataset and JAFFE dataset are experimentally evaluated and the recognition rates of 71.29%, 99.48% and 90.70% are obtained, respectively. Comparative experiments show that the method based on attention mechanism has high recognition accuracy and robustness in facial expression recognition tasks. It has obvious advantages over traditional facial expression recognition methods. The results of this research are expected to have important application value in the fields of affective computing and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Task Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing
abstract: With the development of mobile edge computing (MEC), MEC-based task offloading of vehicle edge computing (VEC) has become popular due to its low delay. However, when vehicle users (VUs) offload data to the edge servers (ESs), user privacy may be leaked. In addition, communication among ESs can also threaten the privacy of VUs. Therefore, a five-objective optimization model including time delay of VLCU, time delay of ES, energy consumption, load balancing, and privacy protection degree is constructed. To solve the above model, an improved CMA-ES algorithm based on triple analysis decision variable grouping strategy (TADG-CMA-ES) is proposed. To improve the dimension reduction performance of the algorithm, the variables in divided subgroups are further grouped according to the convergence relevance degrees (CRD) of the variables.

articleTitle: Verification and Accuracy Check of Luminance and Illuminance Measurements using a Commercial IP Camera Applied as an HDR Vision Sensor
abstract: This study verifies and checks the accuracy of luminance and illuminance from high dynamic range images (HDRI) generated by a commercial IP camera compared to measurement devices. The statistical analysis indicates that measuring luminance using the calibration method with a luminance meter is comparable with measurement results using a luminance meter, with average relative error in the range of 5–23%, whereas illuminance measurement using the equation method is in line with the measurement using an illuminance meter, with an average relative error range of 1–11%. Regarding the accuracy of the HDRI method, using digital cameras is in the range of 5–27%, which is still acceptable.

articleTitle: Research on Algorithm for Small Object Head Pose Estimation
abstract: As a branch of computer vision, head pose estimation is defined as inferring the direction of a person’s head based on a given image, including the three-dimensional vector of pitch, yaw, and roll. In images captured at a distance, the head area of pedestrians is often small and occupies few pixels. It is difficult to accurately determine the head pose or face orientation with only ordinary target detection algorithms and head pose estimation models. Therefore, this paper proposes a three-stage detection method for small targets, which is suitable for head recognition and head pose estimation of low-resolution pedestrian heads in images captured at a distance. Firstly, this paper refers to the YOLO v5 target detection model and incorporates the advantages of multiple advanced small target detection algorithms to build a small target head detection model, SHDN. Secondly, this paper trains a head pose estimation model, SHPEN, based on multi-stage soft regression, which uses a dual-stream heterogeneous network for multi-stage feature extraction and incorporates the SAM spatial attention mechanism in the feature mapping stage. Finally, this paper trains a super-resolution reconstruction model to generate high-resolution images from low-resolution small-target head images. The high-resolution images generated by the super-resolution reconstruction model are output to the head pose estimation model, which significantly improves the prediction accuracy of the head estimation model for small targets.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Model for Multiclass Image Classification Using Quantum CNN
abstract: Technological developments in machine learning have opened up new avenues of advancement almost in every sector. The main challenge is communicating effectively with machines and enhancing their classification abilities. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a deep learning technique in pattern recognition that effectively utilizes data correlation information. In contrast, CNN can only train effectively if the data or model dimension is manageable. Quantum CNN (QCNN) offers a new approach to this problem using quantum computing techniques to enhance the functionality of the classical CNN model. This research article provides an overview of the implementation of deep learning with quantum computing models for image classification. The paper also discusses the modelling approach for CNN in classical and quantum domains. In this paper, we present a model for multiclass image classification using the traditional CNN and the CNN with the quantum layer using the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets. The simulation results show that the proposed QCNN model has lower loss and comparatively more enhanced performance than the traditional CNN model. Also, the proposed model performs relatively better when compared with recent state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Vehicle Flow Prediction at Checkpoint Considering Trajectory Based on Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Network1
abstract: In response to the problem that the current shortterm checkpoint traffic flow prediction model does not consider the trajectory of traffic flow, a convolutional neural network(CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) model Trajectory-CNNLSTM( Tr-CNN-LSTM) based on traffic flow trajectory is proposed. Using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to capture the implicit spatial features of traffic flow between checkpoints, solving the phenomenon of “translation” of traffic flow caused by external factors. By combining the Markov k-order transition probability matrix, long and short-term memory network is used to capture the spatiotemporal characteristics of checkpoint traffic flow. This model can make good predictions on checkpoint traffic flow data with spatiotemporal correlation, and obtain good prediction results by using the checkpoint traffic flow dataset of China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City for testing.

articleTitle: Detection of Epileptic EEG Signals Based on an Improved AFSA-GA Algorithm
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder that occurs worldwide and is characterized by sudden abnormal electrical discharges in the brain. The main benefit of detecting epileptic seizures through electroencephalogram (EEG) is to assist in the evaluation and diagnosis of epilepsy patients. The aim of this study is to establish a hybrid model based on an improved artificial fish swarm algorithm (AFSA) and genetic algorithm (GA) to determine the optimal feature combination for detecting epileptic seizures. Firstly, the geometric features of ten epilepsy EEG signals were extracted using the second-order difference plot (SODP) method across the entire frequency range. Then, an optimization algorithm for feature selection, called AFSA-GA, was proposed by combining the improved AFSA with GA, which was based on a food strategy-based update step. Finally, the feature combination was inputted into a naive Bayes classifier for identifying epileptic and non-epileptic seizures. The proposed method achieved a classification accuracy of 92.94% using a ten-fold cross-validation strategy in frequency band crossing, and is an effective approach for detecting epilepsy that can assist clinicians in quickly diagnosing epilepsy based on SODP analysis and feature selection optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Shared Bike Demand Prediction Based on Multi-Scale ABiLSTM
abstract: In recent years, more and more shared bicycles have entered people’s lives and gradually integrated into the urban traffic structure. However, the problem of imbalance between supply and demand of shared bicycles has always existed. In order to improve the accuracy of bike-sharing demand prediction, A Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network with Multi-Scale Attention Mechanism (MS-ABiLSTM) is proposed. It extracts the time series dependence of different scales through BiLSTM at different scales, and analyzes the influence of various external features on the prediction effect through experiments. The attention mechanism is used to screen the key features of different scales. MAE, MAPE and RMSE are selected to evaluate the prediction accuracy of the proposed model. Compared with the baselines, the experimental results show that the proposed model has the best prediction effect.

articleTitle: 3D Trajectory Planning of Manipulator Based on Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the factory needs to assemble different parts, the ant colony algorithm was used to find a shortest path from many feasible trajectories through multi-objective search as the running trajectory of the manipulator. The obtained path can minimize the movement time of the manipulator and improve the work efficiency. The three-dimensional simulation model of the workspace was established by the grid method, and the simulation was carried out by MATLAB. The results shown the effectiveness of the ant colony algorithm.

articleTitle: Rate Control Method for Video Encoders Operating in Industrial Environments
abstract: Video coding technology aims to reduce the bandwidth needed for video transmission and storage while maintaining the maximum possible video content quality. Rate Control (RC) is the mechanism designed for keeping the compressed rate at some predefined level. While in generic video coding, this has been thoroughly investigated in the past, in industrial computer vision applications using fixed cameras, there are not many efficient solutions capable of reaching the target rate in a fast and efficient manner. This paper proposes a RC method specifically tailored for industrial applications where the variability of the visual content is low and transmission to central servers is prone to errors and losses. The proposed algorithm is adaptive to the scene to be encoded through a startup procedure that builds default rate-quantization functions. Then, in normal operation, these functions are used to determine the quantization parameter that produces the best matching rate considering the predefined target, which can be dynamically defined from network or storage constraints. The results show that steady-state operation is achieved with low absolute error (1.08%) with respect to the target bitrate (BR) and also with fast setting time when abrupt changes are imposed. Overall the proposed method is flexible enough to match the requirements of a wide variety of industrial applications, namely those where remote video should be delivered in compressed format for cloud processing or storage servers.

articleTitle: Secure Reversible Data Hiding in Images with Scalable Capacity
abstract: In available reversible data hiding methods, the capacity of hidden information is basically fixed when the host media is fixed, that is, the capacity lacks scalability. In order to enhance the security of hidden data, encryption technology is often combined with reversible data-hiding methods. However, commercial encryption algorithms due to their complexity will increase the burden, making it difficult to achieve real-time data processing on simple devices. This paper aims to propose a secure fusion of multiple sensitive data, such as various temporal sensing data, by the combination of reversible image data hiding and lightweight encryption technology, achieving a scalable capacity of hidden data. Specifically, the image is divided into non-overlapping sub-blocks, and the number of blocks is calculated based on the amount of data to be hidden. Then, reversible data hiding is performed independently on each block based on block histogram shifting. Using the international standard test images as the host carriers, the feasibility of the scheme is verified through experiments, and the relationship between the number of image blocks and the amount of data that can be hidden, as well as the number of image blocks and the fidelity of the steganographic image is revealed. Although this paper introduces grayscale images as carriers, the proposed algorithms and conclusions are fully applicable to color images.

articleTitle: Exhibition Design of Marine Culture Theme Exhibition Hall Under Interactive Experience
abstract: Marine culture theme display is an artistic and interesting activity. Under the interactive experience, people can interact with each other through virtual scenes. It can not only show the excellent traditional national arts and crafts in the history of our country and the world, but also has great significance in protecting our precious resources and promoting cultural exchanges. This paper expounds the problems existing in the display design of the marine culture theme exhibition hall from three aspects. The first part mainly introduces the current research on overseas sightseeing buildings in China. The second part gives a brief overview of the current exhibition and interactive experience at home and abroad, as well as the connotation of the concept of “virtual reality”. The third part analyzes and summarizes some problems in the construction and development of the marine museum. From the experiment of the marine culture theme display design model under the interactive experience, it can be concluded that, with the support of virtual reality technology and the assistance of digital equipment, the simulation of massive scenes was restored, and the marine culture display interactive experience effect was good, which could efficiently interact with tourists.

articleTitle: Automatic Schizophrenia Detection from Scalp EEG Using CNN with Wide Convolutional Kernel and ELM
abstract: Detection of schizophrenia is of great significance in clinical practice. In conventional machine learning methods, manual feature extraction is required, which is a hard and time-consuming task. This paper proposes a hybrid model consisting of a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a wide convolution kernel and an extreme learning machine (ELM). By changing the size of the convolution kernel to form a suitable wide convolution kernel, and automatically extracting and optimizing the features of the scalp electroencephalogram (EEG), the performance of the model is effectively improved and accurate detection of schizophrenia is achieved. The input of this model is the original multi-channel EEG picture after short-time Fourier transform, and the output are two types of classification labels for schizophrenia and healthy people. In the end, the detection accuracy of schizophrenia reached 95.59%. This model has a powerful advantage in detecting schizophrenia.

articleTitle: Emotion recognition based on CNN-SVM from EEG signals
abstract: Emotion recognition is an important research directions in the field of artificial intelligence. In this paper, we adopted deep learning methods to try to improve the performance of emotion recognition. First, we designed an experiment to induce three different emotions by video footage and collected corresponding EEG signals. Then, CNN-SVM algorithms were adopted to classify positive, neutral and negative emotions. Finally, the recognition performance of CNN-SVM for three-class emotion recognition was verified. It is found that CNN-SVM achieves a highest recognition accuracy of 99.98% and an average recognition accuracy of 98.53%, which is better than CNN alone.

articleTitle: Features Extraction of Different Emotional based on Brain Rhythm
abstract: Emotions are an essential part of human physiological performance. Therefore, the study of emotion recognition is extremely relevant in both practical applications and theoretical research. Based on the electroencephalogram (EEG) data we collected, this paper explored the differences from five different characteristics among the coefficient of variation (CV) , power spectral density (PSD) , differential entropy (DE) , approximate entropy (AE) , and permutation entropy (PE) of three emotions at different rhythms, analyzed the activity of each brain region under different emotions. Finally, this paper also compares the classification accuracy of single features and combined features. The experimental results reveal that emotions are more strongly correlated with Beta and Gamma bands; temporal lobe regions are most active in emotion-related brain activity; and the accuracy of combined features is higher than the accuracy of single feature classification. The experiment conclusively demonstrates that effective feature extraction and selection have far-reaching implications for emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Review of Technologies of Intelligent Development of Airport Complex Operation System
abstract: When the airport is understood as a space concept, airports operation involves many businesses. The critical point of airport intelligence is the technical roadmap, especially for the core business. This paper introduces the intelligent perception of the subjects in airport operation activities, the intelligent analysis of airport operation scenes, and the intelligent decision of the management of airport operation activities based on the classification of application situations. Combined with the application, this paper analysis the breakthrough and bottleneck of new technologies. Finally, this paper summarizes the common problems of intelligent upgrading of airport operation systems.

articleTitle: CoomFL:Improving Global and Local Model Coordination Strategies for Heterogeneous Medical Image Tasks in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning has been widely applied in medical image processing tasks as a new collaborative learning strategy. However, the heterogeneity of image data between different institutions leads to distribution differences, which damage the performance of the joint model. Previous research has mainly addressed the drift issue caused by distribution differences through local or global processing, but there is still significant room for improvement in jointly addressing drifts generated by local and global coupling. To address this issue, we have designed a new coordination framework called CoomFL. First, we employed an image amplitude normalization strategy to generate a more coordinated feature space at the local client, reducing drift in local updates. Next, we designed a parameter perturbation term based on the coordinated feature space and the idea of generating adversarial images to construct a more easily aggregated client model. We then designed a coordinated momentum gradient update strategy for global and local models to reduce the differences between global and local updates. During parameter aggregation, we also designed a weight penalty strategy. Our perturbation strategy and coordinated momentum update strategy jointly promote model aggregation, reducing the gap between global model parameters and local model parameters, while guiding the model towards the optimal solution in a global sense. Under the influence of the aggregation weight penalty, our model can also control the stability of the optimization process. We conducted multiple experiments on medical image classification and segmentation tasks, and the results show that CoomFL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of convergence and accuracy in tasks such as image classification. Specifically, CoomFL ensures that the model performance has a lower performance difference in federated learning tasks with heterogeneous clients.

articleTitle: Compressed Sensing Algorithms Applied to Ill-posed CT Image Reconstructions
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effectiveness of a novel nonlinear filter based compressed sensing algorithm (CS) applied to ill-posed computed tomography (CT) image reconstruction. Multi-detector CT (MDCT) images of maxillofacial region were used. Image reconstructions were made under two scenarios, sparse-view and low-dose. Reconstruction outcomes were compared for CS versus traditional filtered back-projection (FBP) and algebraic reconstruction technique (ART). Image projection data were from 180, 90, 45, and 36 degree rotations. The convergence property of CS was verified. Reconstructed image quality was objectively evaluated by root mean error and peak signal-to-noise ratio. The reconstruction results showed that CS performed equally with FBP and ART for 180 degrees of rotation, where there was no missing information; However, CS outperformed FBP and ART for image quality when the volume of view was achieved from less than a 180 degree imaging rotation. CS also outperformed FBP and ART for noise contaminated projection data resulting from low radiation exposures. Advanced nonlinear based CS compensated for and removed isolated noise points. It can be concluded that CS was superior to FBP and ART for image quality with sparse data capture due to angular rotations of less than 180 degrees, and also in low dose scenarios. By permitting shorter scan rotations and lower dose parameters, CS reconstruction has the potential to reduce radiation dose during MDCT imaging.

articleTitle: Characteristics Analysis and Classification of Foot Autonomic Movements Based on EEG Signals
abstract: To improve the effectiveness of rehabilitation for stroke patients, active training can be used to treat and recover patients’ foot dyskinesia. Recognizing the characteristics of different foot motion states is an important part of active rehabilitation for stroke patients. In this study, EEG signals were collected during three different foot actions (foot at rest, 15 ° stretched and 45° stretched) to conduct a classification study on the EEG signals of different voluntary movements of the right foot. Features of autonomous action EEG signals were extracted and support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were both used for classification. Brain topographic maps and time-frequency maps were utilized to display the characteristics of EEG data. The ground averaged time-frequency map and brain topographic map revealed that the ERD (Event-Related Desynchronization) characteristics of the stretched feet at 45 ° were more obvious than those of the stretched feet at 15°, while the ERD characteristics of the stretched feet at 15° were more obvious than those in the resting state. The classification results showed that the RF algorithm achieved higher classification accuracy (81.89%) compared to the SVM algorithm (74.93%) among the three different action states. The RF classification algorithm was found to be more suitable for the classification of different foot movements with a classification result that was 6.97% higher than that of SVM. Moreover, 90% of the subjects using the RF algorithm achieved an accuracy score of more than 75%. These findings highlight the potential of identifying different voluntary movements of the foot by classifying the characteristics of EEG signals and using them as a basis for the rehabilitation effect evaluation of stroke patients.

articleTitle: Object Tracking with Restrain Learning Anomaly and Adaptive Feature Fusion
abstract: The object tracking algorithm is prone to tracking drift in complex scenes, which lead to abnormal learning of the algorithm. Aiming at this problem, Adaptive feature fusion object tracking to suppress learning anomaly was proposed. Firstly, based on the Staple algorithm, a temporal regularization term was added to control the intensity of the time penalty by using the change of the response value to suppress the learning anomaly of the algorithm. Secondly, the Bhattacharyya coefficient was used to calculate the similarity between the foreground and background color histograms of each frame in real-time. And then the similarity and the fusion coefficient were combined into a fusion factor, and the optimal fusion factor could be obtained by using the log loss function to achieve better feature fusion for each frame. Finally, the method of alternating direction multipliers was used to optimize and solve the correlation filter model for improving the speed of the algorithm. The experimental results on the datasets OTB 100, Temple Color 128, and LaSOT demonstrated the effectiveness and robustness of the object tracking algorithm with suppress learning anomaly and adaptive feature fusion.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Online Brain-Computer Interface System Based on MI-mVEP
abstract: In this study, a hybrid online brain-computer interface (BCI) system was established to address the issue of low recognition accuracy and limited imagery tasks in motor imagery (MI) based on BCI systems. This hybrid system utilized both MI and motion-onset visual evoked potential (mVEP). After simultaneously acquiring MI and mVEP potentials and electroencephalogram (EEG) signal preprocessing, the filter bank common spatial pattern (FBCSP) algorithm was used to extract MI and mVEP features. These features were then employed to construct training set feature vectors. The training set feature vectors of MI and mVEP signals were classified using the backpropagation (BP) neural network and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms, respectively. Based on the established classification model, single test data were recognized online, and the results were fed back to subjects in real-time via block moving routes. The presented system can realize five different block moving paths, with faster moving effects achieved when the system induces MI and mVEP potential simultaneously along the lower left or lower right diagonal path. The experimental results showed that the average classification accuracies of the lower left and lower right diagonal moving effects are up to 84.53% and 84.60%, respectively. These results indicate that this study effectively controls the fast-moving blocks in the online BCI system of MI-mVEP, providing a theoretical basis and experimental support for the research of a hybrid online BCI system based on MI-mVEP. In summary, the proposed system has demonstrated improved performance through the combination of simultaneous MI and mVEP potential utilization and efficient classification algorithms, with promising future applications in BCI research.

articleTitle: Probability-Corrected Overlapping Community Detection Algorithm Based on GCN
abstract: Recently, graph convolutional networks(GCN) have shown great potential in graph-related tasks. Existing models combining community affiliation graph models and graph neural networks have achieved good results in overlapping community detection tasks. However, these models ignore the heterogeneity of node connection probabilities, which violates the laws of real networks. To address this issue, we propose an extension of the existing models that demonstrates how to consider the heterogeneity of probabilities, resulting in an improved objective function. We also design a community affiliation graph model that estimates node-pair connection probabilities in overlapping community networks based on the community affiliation matrix. We use the traditional NOCD model to generate the community affiliation matrix to estimate the probability for community detection tasks. Normalized mutual information (NMI) is used as the evaluation metric to assess the accuracy of the algorithm. Through experimental evaluation, the probability-corrected model shows significant improvement in performance on real networks compared to the uncorrected model.

articleTitle: Custom AI Streaming Accelerator Architecture
abstract: In this paper, we study the common architectures of deep learning accelerators and analysis their efficiency. Then we propose a novel Custom AI Streaming Accelerator (CAISA) architecture for processing deep learning applications. This idea is to minimize the overhead of instruction execution and data load/store such that the computation units are constantly busy working. This architecture has been applied in commercial products and achieved over 95% chip utilization results.

articleTitle: Detecting Soil Moisture Content Based on Multispectral Images from Unmanned aerial vehicle
abstract: The development of agriculture has been constrained by water shortage, and how to use new technology to detect the soil moisture content condition of farmland in real time is the key to achieve rational planning of agricultural water use. In this study, we use unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to collect canopy multispectral images of corn, cotton and peanut crops, extract spectral reflectance and calculate vegetation indices to construct data sets respectively. Using machine learning algorithms to establish a soil moisture content detection model based on UAV multispectral images to achieve rapid and accurate detection of soil moisture content in agricultural fields. The study set up a reasonable data acquisition scheme for multispectral image acquisition by considering the planting areas of corn, cotton and peanut in the experimental field, soil moisture conditions and flight conditions of the UAV. Using eight parameters as independent variables and soil moisture content as dependent variables, the data sets of the three crops were constructed separately and the training and test sets were divided in the ratio of 7:3. Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Backpropagation Neural Network(BPNN), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), bagging, and XGBoostmodels were built for soil moisture content detection, respectively. 1According to the model evaluation indexes, the Bagging model performed well in the corn multispectral soil moisture content dataset, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, RMSE and RPD reaching 0.809, 0.059 and 2.294, respectively, which can detect soil moisture content more accurately than other models. 2 To investigate whether the soil moisture content detection model established using the corn dataset can be extended to other crops, the In order to investigate whether the soil moisture content detection model developed using the corn dataset can be extended to other crops, the datasets based on multispectral images of cotton and peanut were brought into the model for testing. The results showed that the detection effect of peanut was better than that of cotton, but there was still a big difference between the detection effect of peanut and that of corn. 3The soil moisture content detection models based on multispectral data of cotton and peanut were established separately, and the best detection model for both crops was the GBDT model. The R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, RMSE and RPD of the best detection model for cotton soil moisture content reached 0.752, 0.065 and 2.009, respectively, while the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, RMSE and RPD of the best detection model for peanut soil moisture content reached 0.738, 0.061 and 1.954, respectively, with high detection accuracy. Based on machine learning algorithms, this study builds six models to analyze the multispectral image data acquired by UAV, and also explores the effect of soil moisture content detection for various crops, in order to provide new strategies for future soil moisture content detection methods.
